open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:`domain_models`
open_points.text:
`SourceFile`, what `source_folder` reports about one file to `photo_delivery`. It holds the server path
  of the file and never leaves the service; M02 is the form a caller sees;
open_points.question: What are the exact fields, types and validity conditions of `SourceFile`, including whether it carries the relative name, observed metadata, source id or file signature in addition to the server path?
options: It contains only the server path and every other fact is recomputed.
It is an immutable observation containing the path plus all metadata needed by placement.
It contains a safe path handle and a minimal signature used to detect replacement.
open_points.default_guess: Define an immutable internal value containing the server path, relative name, source id and the metadata/signature needed to detect replacement.

open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:Dependencies
open_points.text:
`system_clock` is the module that `system_clock_backend` generates. `deliverer_api` alone names it, and
hands `utc_now` to an operation as a function that `photo_delivery` calls.
open_points.question: Which module owns the callable contract handed from `deliverer_api` to `photo_delivery`, and what are its parameter name, signature and lifetime?
options: `photo_delivery` owns a per-call callable parameter returning the A7 datetime.
`deliverer_api` owns an application-scoped clock interface passed to every operation.
Operations receive an already-read datetime instead of a callable.
open_points.default_guess: Let `photo_delivery` own a callable parameter named `clock`, returning the A7 datetime, and invoke it exactly once per operation.

open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:Dependencies
open_points.text:
The operations
read the record themselves through `confirmed_connection`, so no module keeps connections in memory.
open_points.question: How is the single connections-file reading carried from `confirmed_connection` to `available_photo_folder` so that the latter cannot reread the file and the operation continues on the original snapshot?
options: One combined object-connections capability performs both confirmation and folder availability checks.
An explicit operation-scoped connections snapshot is returned and passed to both checks.
open_points.default_guess: Have `confirmed_connection` read once and return the validated `ObjectConnection`; require `available_photo_folder` to consume that value without accessing the connections file.

open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:Rules decided across modules
open_points.text: | A5 | rule 9, stored names built only from checked identifiers | `delivery_store` |
open_points.question: How can `delivery_store` establish that the plain-text project and source identifiers it receives were checked, and which module owns that precondition?
options: `photo_delivery` owns validation and passes refined checked-identifier types to `delivery_store`.
`delivery_store` validates again and therefore directly depends on the identifier rules and `SOURCE_ID_FORM`.
The delivery-store contracts state a trusted precondition enforced by `photo_delivery`.
open_points.default_guess: Use refined checked-identifier values created by `photo_delivery` and accepted by `delivery_store`, making the validation boundary structural.

open_points.subject: 30_modules.md:Rules decided across modules
open_points.text: | A7 | rules 1 and 3, the clock and the form of its reading | `system_clock` |
open_points.question: Who owns the parts of A7 rule 3 that use the reading to decide settling status and set `marked_at`, since `system_clock` must not own comparisons and the state otherwise assigns those behaviors to `source_folder` and `photo_delivery`?
options: Split A7 rule 3: `system_clock` owns only the returned datetime form, `source_folder` owns settling comparisons, and `photo_delivery` owns `marked_at`.
Let `system_clock` own all of rule 3 and expose higher-level settling and marking operations.
Rewrite A7 rule 3 into separately owned rules before assigning owners.
open_points.default_guess: Split the rule by responsibility, leaving `system_clock` responsible only for producing the correctly formed current time.
